chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah ibn Bidd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the beginning of the time for the two rak'ahs of Fajr, so he said: 'One-sixth of the remaining night.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two voluntary units of prayer performed before the obligatory Fajr prayer
key_terms.سُدُسُ اللَّيْلِ الْبَاقِي: One-sixth of the remaining night, a specific temporal marker for prayer times

ai.seo_question: When does the time for the two rak'ahs of Fajr prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) defines the onset of the time for the two sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr as one-sixth of the remaining night, a calculation that places it slightly before the true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq). This specific timing highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the start of the sunnah period and the obligatory prayer, emphasizing the virtue of performing these voluntary prayers early to secure their acceptance before the adhan. The reference to 'one-sixth' reflects the traditional method of dividing the night into four parts, with this mark serving as a precise temporal boundary for worship.
